alternatives.root_cause: Injected network delay on payment's interface made charges slow enough to exhaust checkout's deadlines.
alternatives.why_not: The traffic-shaping containers in tr_34f3beeb1ba3 were all attached and removed between 00:04 and 01:14, hours before onset, and latency would still leave payment logging and emitting spans, which it does not after 22:31:36.

alternatives.root_cause: checkout itself regressed on a CURRENCY_ADDR environment change and failed its own orchestration.
alternatives.why_not: All CURRENCY_ADDR edits in tr_1aa3b1ec77e0 were applied and reverted in the 05:20-06:48 range, and currency spans inside checkout traces stay sub-millisecond (tr_3fd6b25585e0); nothing changed on checkout near onset.

alternatives.root_cause: A shared messaging or downstream outage stopped order processing for accounting and fraud-detection.
alternatives.why_not: fraud-detection consumed records normally right up to 22:31:35 and logged no connectivity complaints (tr_cc0c1e827cd6); its silence is explained by checkout no longer publishing orders, making it a victim rather than the origin.

verdict.summary: The payment service's process stopped serving at ~22:31:36 — it emitted no further logs, spans or metrics while its callers kept calling — so checkout's Charge calls hung to their deadlines and failed, propagating errors to frontend/email/accounting/fraud-detection.
verdict.reasoning: checkout is the first alerter but its own spans show it as a fan-out orchestrator; its error ratio departs from an exactly-zero baseline at 22:33:46 (tr_a84246b73270). Looking down the call path, payment's last log line is at ~22:31:36 and its newest traced spans are from ~22:31:13 (tr_54dbf8a797cb, tr_677bdd9cde19), with no error-ratio samples at all in the incident window (tr_e387b5261b41) — the service simply stops producing telemetry while load continues. The other dependencies in the same critical path are healthy and still talking: cart logs continuously to 22:40 (tr_e8eb62cce34c) and product-catalog shows a flat zero error ratio (tr_21e7f243b643), so a shared infrastructure fault is unlikely. fraud-detection's consumption stops at the same moment (tr_cc0c1e827cd6), which follows from checkout no longer publishing completed orders rather than from a fault of its own. Payment's change log holds only traffic-shaping attach/remove pairs that ended many hours earlier and were reverted (tr_34f3beeb1ba3), so no artifact or config change explains the onset. Silent process plus hanging callers plus an empty change window is the freeze signature; a partitioned payment would still be writing complaints that it cannot reach anything, and a full disk or corrupt store would produce explicit write/read failures in its own log.
open_questions: Whether payment's socket still accepted connections (true freeze) versus the container exiting — the data shows absence of telemetry but not the socket state.
The exact failure status checkout saw on Charge (deadline exceeded vs connection refused) was not retrieved; checkout emitted no log lines in the window at all.
Why payment's error-ratio series had no samples even in the baseline window, which leaves its pre-incident health unverified by metrics.
What stopped the process — OOM kill, SIGSTOP, or a stuck runtime — no host-level resource evidence was collected.
